ModMetadata.Name: Terraforming Reloaded
ModMetadata.Author: XCeled
ModMetadata.Description:
[h1]Terraform the planet[/h1] In the base game the planet's air never runs out: gas you vent outside vanishes, and gas your base pulls in comes from nowhere. With this mod the planet holds a fixed amount of air. Add or remove enough of the right gases and the outside pressure, temperature, sky and weather change, and stay changed in your save.
[hr][/hr] [h2]Temperature[/h2] The planet's temperature depends on which gases are in the air and how much air there is. [table] [tr][th]Effect[/th][th]Gases[/th][/tr] [tr][td][b]Warms[/b][/td][td]pollutant (strongest), volatiles, carbon dioxide, steam[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]Cools[/b][/td][td]nitrous oxide (strongest), hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]None[/b][/td][td]helium, hydrazine, hydrochloric acid, ozone, silanol[/td][/tr] [/table] [list] [*]The more of a gas there is, the stronger its effect. [*]Thicker air, of any gas, makes days cooler and nights warmer. [*]Breathable air is mostly nitrogen and oxygen, which both cool, so it needs carbon dioxide to stay warm. A breathable Mars needs about 75 moles of carbon dioxide per outdoor cell against 57 of oxygen. [/list]
[hr][/hr] [h2]How it plays[/h2] [list] [*]An endgame project. You need a base that moves gas in bulk: ice mining rockets, gas traders, large vents, tank farms. [*]Venus and Vulcan are hot because of their air. Remove the warming gases and they cool down. [*]Cold worlds warm in stages. A gas that freezes at the current temperature just snows into the ice caps and does nothing. Start with a gas that stays in the air at that temperature, let it warm the planet a little, and the next gas can then stay up too. Nothing that froze on the way is lost: the ice caps release it as the planet warms. [*]The Moon and Mimas start with no air. New air there swings hard between day and night until there is more of it. [*]Storms are milder on a world you have cooled. [*]Storms depend on the air. Remove most of a world's air, or make it temperate, thick and clean, and its own storms stop. Solar storms keep coming unless you turn them off in the settings; on the Moon one gives four times the usual solar power. [*]A world you have not changed behaves exactly as it does without the mod. [*]Custom worlds work. World authors: see WORLDS.md in the mod folder. [/list]
[hr][/hr] [h2]How long it takes[/h2] The [b]Planet size[/b] setting decides the pace. Hours until you can take your helmet off outside: [table] [tr][th]World[/th][th]Terraforming strategy[/th][th]Short 1/100[/th][th]Standard 1/20[/th][th]Long 1/4[/th][th]Unmodded 1/1[/th][/tr] [tr][td]Venus[/td][td]Strip the air, tank what you take[/td][td]8[/td][td]40[/td][td]201[/td][td]806[/td][/tr] [tr][td]The Moon[/td][td]Add gas, nothing to remove[/td][td]15[/td][td]73[/td][td]367[/td][td]1,467[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Mars[/td][td]Add gas, nothing to remove[/td][td]15[/td][td]75[/td][td]376[/td][td]1,503[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Europa[/td][td]Tank the oxygen, warm, put it back[/td][td]44[/td][td]220[/td][td]1,101[/td][td]4,402[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Vulcan[/td][td]Strip the fuel first, then fill[/td][td]44[/td][td]222[/td][td]1,108[/td][td]4,431[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Mimas[/td][td]Warm it in stages, from nothing[/td][td]72[/td][td]360[/td][td]1,802[/td][td]7,208[/td][/tr] [/table] [b]Unmodded[/b] is the planet size the game itself uses. The smaller sizes mean less air in total, so less to move.
[b]The hours count only time spent moving gas.[/b] Adding gas is limited by how fast ice arrives: there is no other source of oxygen, and the carbon dioxide a cold world needs has to be made by burning volatiles. Removing gas is much faster, because a vent draws from the whole planet's air at once. So Venus is quick but still a big project: you need somewhere to store what you take out, about 48 large tanks at Standard size.
[b]Calculated, not measured.[/b] The numbers assume four ice mining rockets (about 330,000 moles of ice an hour) and twenty large powered vents. With half the rockets, every number doubles.
Size changes nothing else: the starting air, pressure and temperature are the same at every size. A save from before you installed the mod keeps the full-size planet until you rescale it.
[hr][/hr] [h2]Console (F3)[/h2] [list] [*][b]terraform[/b] : pressure, temperature, gases, and whether the mod is running [*][b]terraform set[/b] : this world's settings. [b]terraform set <key> <value>[/b] changes one for this world only. Settings that delete something permanently ask you to confirm [*][b]terraform size <share> confirm[/b] : change the planet size, and with it how long terraforming takes. Pressure, mix and temperature stay the same [*][b]terraform reset confirm[/b] : put the planet back the way the world ships. Your base is not touched [*][b]terraform gas add[/b] / [b]remove[/b] : add a gas to the planet or remove one, for testing [*][b]terraform curves export[/b] / [b]reload[/b] : tune the temperature response. See CURVES.md [/list]
[hr][/hr] [h2]Removing it[/h2] The changes are stored in your save, so removing the mod does not undo them. First run [b]terraform reset confirm[/b], save and quit, then disable the mod. If you skip this, a changed world jumps back to its original temperature: a breathable Venus returns to 737 K, and new air on the Moon drops to near absolute zero.
[hr][/hr] [h2]Good to know[/h2] [list] [*]The StationeersLaunchPad config editor sets the defaults for new worlds. Each world then keeps its own settings: change the current world's with [b]terraform set[/b]. [*]The pressure ceiling permanently deletes air above its limit. Leave it at 0 (off) unless you want that. [*]Multiplayer: the host and every player need the mod, same version. The host's settings apply to everyone, and only the host can run [b]terraform size[/b], [b]set[/b], [b]reset[/b] and [b]gas[/b]. [*][b]Experimental, off by default:[/b] [b]terraform set TraceGasGatheringEnabled on[/b] makes a small spill of a gas the planet barely has (for example from a furnace taken apart outside) collect near your base, where it burns off or reaches your filters, instead of spreading thinly over the whole planet for hours. [*][b]Experimental, off by default, enable at your own risk:[/b] [b]terraform set CometsEnabled on[/b] lets rockets cut comets at space map sites and bring them down. Ice comets add gas, mineral comets remove it, and an impact can destroy structures and hurt players near it. [*][b]Off by default:[/b] [b]terraform set SpaceDeletesGas on[/b] deletes gas released at or above 1,000 m, where rockets in space are, instead of letting it drift back down, so a rocket can carry unwanted gas off the world. Deleted gas is gone for good; turning the setting off later does not bring it back. In multiplayer it applies to gas any player vents in space. [*][b]On by default:[/b] rocket engines burn all their propellant, so a 2:1 methane and oxygen mix leaves no oxygen in the exhaust to start fires. If you turn this off after flying, auto-landings can come in too fast; see the readme. [*]Tutorials are not affected. [*]If a game update breaks something the mod depends on, the mod turns itself off and logs why, instead of risking your save. [/list]
[hr][/hr] [b]Requires[/b] [url=https://github.com/StationeersLaunchPad/StationeersLaunchPad]StationeersLaunchPad[/url]
[b]Source, issues and the full readme:[/b] [url=https://github.com/altmank/Stationeers-TerraformingReloaded]github.com/altmank/Stationeers-TerraformingReloaded[/url]
Inspired by Elmotrix's Terraforming Mod. This is a new mod written for the current game, not a port.

ModMetadata.ChangeLog: v0.14.0 - New, off by default: a storm floor and ceiling. terraform set StormFloorKelvin <K> stops a storm taking the planet colder than that (StormCeilingKelvin: hotter). Only the storm's own effect is limited. v0.13.2 - Fixed a crash when rain turns to snow, or snow to rain. v0.13.1 - Clearer config editor text: a world setting there only applies to new worlds; change a world already started with terraform set while playing it.
